motorrad-fahrphysik-01.question: You are riding straight ahead at normal speed and want to initiate a right-hand bend. What is the most effective way to lean the motorcycle into the turn?

options.a: Shift your body weight to the right only, without touching the handlebars
options.b: Briefly press lightly on the right handlebar grip, which tips the bike into a lean to the right
options.c: Pull on the right handlebar end to turn the front fork to the right
options.d: Tap the rear brake briefly so the bike leans on its own

motorrad-fahrphysik-01.explanation: At normal to higher speeds, steering works through countersteering: a brief, light push on the handlebar grip on the side you want to turn towards (here, right) makes the motorcycle lean and turn that way. Body weight alone is not enough to initiate a lean at these speeds, and braking to trigger a lean is dangerous and unpredictable.

motorrad-fahrphysik-02.question: When should you reduce your speed before a tight bend?

options.a: Before you start turning in, so you can ride through the bend at a constant or slightly increasing speed
options.b: Only once you're already mid-corner and notice your speed is too high
options.c: Braking while leaned over is unproblematic as long as you only use the front brake
options.d: It doesn't matter, since modern motorcycles brake equally well at any lean angle

motorrad-fahrphysik-02.explanation: Braking should generally be finished before entering a bend. While leaned over, the available tire grip is already being used for cornering forces; braking on top of that can cause the front wheel to slide out. It is best to ride through the corner at a steady or slightly increasing speed.

motorrad-fahrphysik-03.question: Why does the front brake provide most of the stopping power during hard braking on dry, grippy road surface?

options.a: Because the front wheel generally has a larger tire diameter
options.b: Because the rear brake on motorcycles is legally only allowed to act as a support function
options.c: Because braking shifts weight forward, significantly increasing the load and grip on the front tire
options.d: Because the rear wheel automatically lifts off the ground when braking

motorrad-fahrphysik-03.explanation: During braking, weight transfers dynamically to the front. This increases the load on the front tire, giving it more grip and allowing it to transmit far more braking force than the now-unloaded rear wheel, which can lock up easily under hard braking.

motorrad-fahrphysik-04.question: What benefit does an anti-lock braking system (ABS) provide on a motorcycle during emergency braking?

options.a: It always reduces stopping distance to zero on any surface
options.b: It removes the need to use both brakes
options.c: It automatically increases engine power to maintain balance
options.d: It prevents the wheels from locking up, keeping the bike steerable and stable while braking

motorrad-fahrphysik-04.explanation: ABS stops a wheel from locking and skidding when braking too hard. This keeps the motorcycle stable and steerable even during hard braking, which is especially important on slippery surfaces or in panic situations. Both brakes still need to be actively applied.

motorrad-fahrphysik-05.question: What helps most to keep a motorcycle stable at very low speed, for example when doing a U-turn or maneuvering in a parking lot?

options.a: Gripping the handlebars as tightly as possible with locked-out arms
options.b: Looking well ahead in the direction you want to go, slightly slipping the clutch, and using the rear brake to fine-tune speed
options.c: Keeping your feet off the footpegs at all times in case you need to catch yourself
options.d: Riding as fast as possible, since a motorcycle is always less stable at low speed than at high speed

motorrad-fahrphysik-05.explanation: At low speed, the stabilizing gyroscopic effect of the wheels is minimal, so active balance is needed: looking where you want to go, gently slipping the clutch, and modulating the rear brake help keep the motorcycle calm and controlled.

motorrad-fahrphysik-06.question: You need to cross a short stretch of loose gravel or grit. What is the safest way to handle it?

options.a: Accelerate hard to get across the patch as quickly as possible
options.b: Brake hard as soon as the front wheel reaches the gravel
options.c: Reduce speed beforehand, keep the bike as upright as possible, and ride through calmly and loosely with minimal steering and braking inputs
options.d: Lean over as far as possible so more tire surface makes contact

motorrad-fahrphysik-06.explanation: On loose surfaces, grip is greatly reduced and unpredictable. Slowing down beforehand, staying upright, and avoiding abrupt steering or braking inputs gives the motorcycle the best chance to balance itself through the hazard.

motorrad-fahrphysik-07.question: In the rain, wet leaves are lying on the road, and you also need to ride over a wide painted lane marking. What should you be prepared for?

options.a: Both can be extremely slippery; you should cross these areas as upright as possible, without braking or steering
options.b: Painted markings offer more grip than normal asphalt when wet, because the paint is rough
options.c: Wet leaves increase grip, since they act like an extra rubber layer
options.d: Such spots only matter for car drivers; road surface doesn't matter for motorcycles

motorrad-fahrphysik-07.explanation: Wet leaves and wet lane markings are among the trickiest surfaces for motorcyclists because friction drops sharply there. Such spots should be crossed as upright as possible and without braking or steering inputs, to avoid the front or rear wheel sliding out.

motorrad-fahrphysik-08.question: You need to cross tram tracks that run at an angle to your direction of travel. What is the safest way to cross them?

options.a: Stay as close as possible to a shallow angle along the rails to save time
options.b: If possible, briefly adjust your line to cross the rails at as steep, near right, angle as possible
options.c: Accelerate hard as soon as the front wheel reaches the rail
options.d: Brake on the rails to adjust your speed for crossing

motorrad-fahrphysik-08.explanation: Rails and grooves are extremely slippery, especially when wet. A shallow crossing angle increases the risk that the front wheel gets caught in the groove or slides out. Crossing at as steep, near-perpendicular an angle as possible minimizes this risk; braking directly on the rails should be avoided.

motorrad-fahrphysik-09.question: Why are manhole covers and other metal surfaces on the road a particular risk for motorcyclists?

options.a: They always sit higher than the surrounding road surface and cause a jolt
options.b: They are harmless for motorcycles, since the weight is too low to break through
options.c: Metal surfaces offer significantly less grip than asphalt, especially when wet, and can cause a sudden loss of traction
options.d: They are only slippery on dry roads

motorrad-fahrphysik-09.explanation: Metal covers such as manhole lids are considerably slicker than asphalt when wet. Braking or leaning while crossing them risks a sudden loss of grip. Such spots should be crossed as upright as possible and without braking or strong steering input.

motorrad-fahrphysik-10.question: Which statement about the gyroscopic effect of the spinning wheels is correct?

options.a: It makes a motorcycle especially prone to tipping over at very low speed
options.b: It makes steering input completely unnecessary, the bike balances itself in any situation
options.c: It only occurs when the engine is switched off
options.d: It increasingly stabilizes the motorcycle as speed rises, which is why an active steering input (countersteering) is needed at higher speed to change direction

motorrad-fahrphysik-10.explanation: The rotating wheels act like gyroscopes: the faster they spin, the more strongly they stabilize the motorcycle in its current orientation. This makes riding at higher speed feel steadier, but it also means a deliberate, brief steering input (countersteering) is needed to overcome that stability and change direction.

motorrad-fahrphysik-11.question: You are riding in strong, gusty crosswind, for example on a bridge or at a gap in roadside trees. What is the correct response?

options.a: Ride as fast as possible so the wind has less time to affect the motorcycle
options.b: Reduce speed, hold the handlebars loosely but securely, and be prepared for sudden gusts at open spots
options.c: Grip the handlebars as tightly as possible with your arms fully locked out
options.d: Always move as far right as possible, regardless of wind direction

motorrad-fahrphysik-11.explanation: Gusty crosswind can suddenly push a motorcycle sideways. Reduced speed provides more reaction time, a relaxed but firm grip lets the bike make small corrective movements on its own, and riders should anticipate a gust at bridges or gaps in tree lines before it hits.

motorrad-fahrphysik-12.question: A large truck is overtaking you, or you are overtaking it, on the motorway. What should you be prepared for?

options.a: A sudden gust or suction effect that can briefly pull or push the motorcycle sideways, especially when passing the rear of the vehicle
options.b: No effect at all, since large vehicles actually calm the surrounding air
options.c: That the effect only occurs below 30 km/h
options.d: That this effect only happens with oncoming traffic, never when overtaking in the same direction

motorrad-fahrphysik-12.explanation: Large vehicles create a bow wave and a suction effect at the rear that can push a motorcycle sideways when passing. A firm but relaxed grip on the handlebars, adequate lateral distance, and anticipating this effect help you react safely instead of being caught off guard.

motorrad-fahrphysik-13.question: You are riding in a group of motorcycles. How should your following distance to the rider ahead compare to riding alone?

options.a: It can be noticeably smaller, since group members are used to riding together
options.b: It stays exactly the same regardless of riding alone or in a group
options.c: It should generally be larger, since your view of the traffic situation ahead of the group is more limited and you also need to be prepared for the reactions of other group members
options.d: It can be reduced as much as desired as long as everyone rides at the same speed

motorrad-fahrphysik-13.explanation: In a group, your view of potential hazards ahead of the group is more limited, and a sudden braking maneuver by a rider further ahead can trigger a chain reaction. A larger following distance gives you more time to react to such situations.

motorrad-fahrphysik-14.question: What is the advantage of a staggered riding formation (for example, one motorcycle on the left, the next on the right within the lane) when riding in a group?

options.a: It allows reducing the distance to the motorcycle directly ahead in the same half of the lane without any downside
options.b: It creates more lateral space and better mutual visibility, and it gives each rider their own room to maneuver
options.c: It is only allowed on motorways and forbidden on rural roads
options.d: It replaces the need for turn signals when the whole group changes lanes

motorrad-fahrphysik-14.explanation: The staggered formation increases the lateral gap between motorcycles, improves mutual visibility, and gives each rider room to maneuver if needed. The distance to the motorcycle actually ahead in the same half of the lane must still remain adequately large.

motorrad-fahrphysik-15.question: How do you achieve the shortest stopping distance during emergency braking on a dry road?

options.a: Apply both brakes firmly but progressively at the same time, with the front brake providing the larger share of the braking force
options.b: Use only the rear brake, since a locked front wheel inevitably causes a crash
options.c: Use only the front brake, and generally avoid the rear brake
options.d: First pull in the clutch and coast, only braking afterwards

motorrad-fahrphysik-15.explanation: The shortest stopping distance is achieved by applying both brakes simultaneously and progressively. Because weight shifts forward under braking, the front brake carries the larger share of the deceleration, with the rear brake adding extra stopping power. Using only one brake wastes braking force and unnecessarily lengthens the stopping distance.

motorrad-schutzausruestung-01.question: Who must wear a suitable protective helmet when riding a motorcycle?

options.a: Only the rider, passengers are exempt
options.b: Only on trips outside built-up areas
options.c: Both the rider and every passenger, regardless of the distance traveled
options.d: Only at speeds above 50 km/h

motorrad-schutzausruestung-01.explanation: The helmet requirement applies equally to the rider and all passengers, regardless of the distance traveled or speed. Even on short trips there is a significant risk of head injury, which is why the requirement applies without exception.

motorrad-schutzausruestung-02.question: Which statement about correctly wearing a protective helmet is true?

options.a: It is enough to put the helmet on loosely, the chin strap doesn't need to be fastened
options.b: The helmet must fit properly and the chin strap must be securely fastened so it doesn't shift or come off in a crash
options.c: A helmet that is too large is not a problem as long as it stays on the head
options.d: The chin strap is purely for comfort and has no safety-related purpose

motorrad-schutzausruestung-02.explanation: A helmet only offers reliable protection if it fits properly and the chin strap is securely fastened. A loose helmet or an unfastened chin strap can slip off the head in a crash, exactly when protection matters most.

motorrad-schutzausruestung-03.question: Your helmet hit the asphalt in a crash, but there is no visible external damage. What should you do?

options.a: Replace the helmet anyway, since the inner protective structure can be damaged and lose its effectiveness even without visible damage
options.b: Keep using the helmet as long as it looks undamaged from the outside
options.c: Only replace the helmet if there is a visible crack in the chin strap
options.d: Simply have the helmet repainted, this fully restores its protective effect

motorrad-schutzausruestung-03.explanation: The inner cushioning structure of a helmet is designed to deform on impact and absorb energy. This deformation is often not visible from the outside, but it significantly reduces protection in a subsequent crash. After a significant impact, a helmet should generally be replaced.

motorrad-schutzausruestung-04.question: Why is such importance placed on dedicated motorcycle jackets and trousers made of leather or abrasion-resistant textile?

options.a: They primarily improve aerodynamics and therefore top speed
options.b: They remove the need for a protective helmet on short trips
options.c: In a crash, they protect the skin from abrading on the asphalt for much longer than ordinary everyday clothing
options.d: They exist purely for rain protection and have no effect on injuries in a crash

motorrad-schutzausruestung-04.explanation: Unlike car occupants, motorcyclists have no protective safety cell around them. If a rider falls and slides across the road, abrasion-resistant leather or specialized textile material holds up far longer than ordinary everyday clothing like jeans, which can wear through in a fraction of a second.

motorrad-schutzausruestung-05.question: What is the purpose of the protectors (impact-absorbing padding) in motorcycle jackets and trousers?

options.a: They exist purely to improve the fit of the clothing
options.b: If present, they remove the need for a protective helmet
options.c: They mainly serve as insulation against the cold in winter
options.d: They are meant to cushion impacts at the shoulders, elbows, knees, and back in a crash and distribute the energy better

motorrad-schutzausruestung-05.explanation: Protectors are made of impact-absorbing material that spreads and cushions the energy of an impact at especially vulnerable body areas such as shoulders, elbows, knees, and the back. They do not replace a helmet but complement the protective effect of the rest of the gear.

motorrad-schutzausruestung-06.question: Why are sturdy motorcycle boots and gloves recommended instead of ordinary shoes and thin gloves?

options.a: They are generally lighter than regular shoes and therefore improve acceleration
options.b: They additionally protect the ankles and wrists and offer a better grip on the gear lever, brake lever, and handlebars
options.c: They are legally mandatory and therefore only a formality with no practical benefit
options.d: They mainly improve the rider's outward appearance

motorrad-schutzausruestung-06.explanation: Ankles and wrists are particularly vulnerable to injury in a crash and are protected by sturdy boots and gloves. They also improve grip on the controls and protect the skin from abrasion and cold.

motorrad-schutzausruestung-07.question: What benefit does light-colored or reflective clothing, or a reflective helmet, offer motorcyclists?

options.a: It only improves how warm the rider feels in sunshine
options.b: It is purely cosmetic and has no effect on safety
options.c: It increases the likelihood of being noticed in time by other road users, especially at dusk, in rain, or in poor visibility
options.d: It removes the requirement to ride with the headlight switched on

motorrad-schutzausruestung-07.explanation: Motorcyclists are already harder to spot due to their narrow silhouette. Light-colored, reflective clothing and a conspicuous helmet stand out better against the background and significantly improve visibility, especially at dusk, in rain, or fog - but they do not replace the requirement to ride with lights on.

motorrad-schutzausruestung-08.question: Why are motorcyclists often overlooked by car drivers even though the driver was looking in their direction (the so-called 'looked but failed to see' effect)?

options.a: From a distance, a motorcycle occupies a much smaller portion of the visual field than a car, making it easier for the brain to overlook or misjudge its speed and distance
options.b: Motorcycles are always faster than cars and are therefore physically impossible to perceive
options.c: By law, motorcyclists have no obligation to be seen
options.d: This phenomenon only affects novice car drivers; experienced drivers are not affected by it

motorrad-schutzausruestung-08.explanation: Because a motorcycle has a much smaller silhouette than a car, it is harder to perceive from a distance. The brain often expects a car and overlooks the smaller object, or underestimates how quickly it is approaching. This effect occurs even in attentive drivers of any experience level, which is why motorcyclists should pay particular attention to their own visibility.

motorrad-schutzausruestung-09.question: You are approaching a junction where a vehicle is waiting to pull out. How should you best position yourself within your lane to be seen more easily?

options.a: Always exactly in the middle of the lane, regardless of the traffic situation
options.b: In a position where you appear as early as possible in the waiting driver's field of view and are not hidden by other vehicles or a blind spot
options.c: As close as possible to the right edge of the road, to leave as much space as possible for oncoming traffic
options.d: Your position within the lane has no effect at all on your own visibility

motorrad-schutzausruestung-09.explanation: Your position within your own lane affects how early and how well a waiting driver perceives the motorcycle. A sensible line avoids disappearing behind parked vehicles, bushes, or another vehicle's blind spot, giving the motorcyclist more reaction time and visibility.

motorrad-schutzausruestung-10.question: Must motorcycles ride with their lights on even during the day in good visibility?

options.a: No, the light may generally stay off during the day to save the battery
options.b: Yes, motorcycles must always ride with dipped headlights on, even in daylight, so they are more visible to other road users
options.c: Only when street lighting is switched on
options.d: Only outside built-up areas; riding with lights on during the day is forbidden within built-up areas

motorrad-schutzausruestung-10.explanation: Because motorcycles are easier to overlook due to their narrow silhouette, they must always ride with their dipped headlight on, regardless of the time of day. This significantly improves their visibility, especially in situations with a lot of background traffic or backlighting.

motorrad-schutzausruestung-11.question: What should you pay particular attention to when choosing motorcycle clothing for a longer ride in changeable, cool, and rainy weather?

options.a: As thin and airy clothing as possible, to maximize freedom of movement
options.b: Purely fashionable aspects, since function is secondary on short trips
options.c: Clothing in as dark a color as possible, so dirt doesn't show
options.d: Wind- and waterproof, breathable clothing with layers that can be adjusted as needed, along with adequate thermal protection

motorrad-schutzausruestung-11.explanation: In cool, changeable weather, the wind chill from riding further cools the body. Wind- and waterproof, breathable layered clothing keeps the rider dry and warm and can be adapted to changing conditions, which helps maintain concentration and therefore riding safety.

motorrad-schutzausruestung-12.question: Why is alcohol consumption particularly dangerous when riding a motorcycle, compared to driving a car?

options.a: Because riding a motorcycle requires constant active balance, which is impaired even by small amounts of alcohol, whereas a car remains balanced on its own
options.b: Because motorcycles have no brakes, so any impairment immediately leads to a crash
options.c: Because alcohol is punished more severely by law for motorcyclists, but has no different effect on riding ability than on driving a car
options.d: Because, unlike car drivers, motorcyclists are essentially unaffected by alcohol since fresh air neutralizes its effect

motorrad-schutzausruestung-12.explanation: A car stands stable on four wheels by itself, while a motorcycle must be actively balanced at all times. Alcohol impairs exactly the abilities needed for this - sense of balance, reaction time, and coordination - much more severely even at small amounts than it does for driving a car.

motorrad-schutzausruestung-13.question: Why is fatigue particularly risky for motorcyclists?

options.a: Fatigue only affects reaction time in traffic, never balance
options.b: Fatigue generally affects motorcyclists less than car drivers, because the wind keeps them awake
options.c: A brief microsleep or lapse in concentration can directly cause a loss of balance and a crash, whereas a car stays upright on its own even during a moment of inattention
options.d: Fatigue only matters on night rides; there is no elevated risk during the day

motorrad-schutzausruestung-13.explanation: Because a motorcycle requires constant active balance, even a very brief lapse in attention or consciousness due to fatigue can lead to an immediate crash. A car, on the other hand, stays stable on the road even during a brief lapse in attention. Wind alone does not keep a rider awake and does not protect against fatigue.

motorrad-schutzausruestung-14.question: Why should you not use a heavily tinted (dark) helmet visor at night or in poor visibility?

options.a: A tinted visor is actually beneficial at night because it prevents glare from your own headlight
options.b: A heavily tinted visor reduces light transmission so much in the dark that it significantly worsens your view of the road, obstacles, and other road users
options.c: Visor tint has no effect on vision at all, it is purely a matter of style
options.d: A tinted visor is legally required at night to protect the eyes

motorrad-schutzausruestung-14.explanation: A dark-tinted visor is intended for use in bright daylight and glare. In the dark or poor visibility it lets through too little light, meaning the road, obstacles, and other road users are recognized much later - a significant safety risk. At night, a clear or only lightly tinted visor belongs on the helmet.

motorrad-schutzausruestung-15.question: Why is ordinary everyday clothing, such as plain jeans and a hoodie, discouraged as the sole protective clothing when riding a motorcycle?

options.a: Such fabrics typically only withstand a fraction of a second of sliding across asphalt in a crash before wearing through, leaving the skin unprotected
options.b: Everyday clothing is legally forbidden and automatically results in losing your driving license
options.c: Everyday clothing offers exactly the same protection as certified motorcycle gear, but is less comfortable
options.d: The only downside of everyday clothing is that it is too warm in summer

motorrad-schutzausruestung-15.explanation: Tests show that ordinary cotton fabrics like jeans wear through extremely quickly when sliding across a rough road surface, often within a fraction of a second, leaving the skin unprotected. Purpose-built motorcycle clothing made from abrasion-resistant materials, by contrast, holds up far longer and protects against severe abrasion injuries.

motorrad-verkehrsverhalten-01.question: How should you position yourself within your lane as a motorcyclist?

options.a: Always exactly in the middle of the lane, since the surface grip is best there
options.b: Offset depending on traffic conditions, to see and be seen well and to avoid the often oily centre strip
options.c: As far right as possible regardless of visibility or road surface
options.d: Always at the far left edge of the lane to make overtaking easier

motorrad-verkehrsverhalten-01.explanation: Motorcyclists should adapt their lane position to the traffic situation to maximise visibility and be seen by others. The centre of the lane is often slippery due to oil and rubber residue and should be avoided.

motorrad-verkehrsverhalten-02.question: You are stuck in slow-moving queued traffic on your motorcycle. Are you allowed to filter between the lanes past the stationary vehicles?

options.a: Yes, this is expressly permitted for motorcycles in Germany
options.b: Yes, as long as you keep to walking pace
options.c: No, motorcyclists must also keep to their lane and are not allowed to ride between rows of vehicles
options.d: Yes, as long as you do not touch any wing mirrors

motorrad-verkehrsverhalten-02.explanation: Lane splitting is not permitted in Germany. Motorcyclists are subject to the same lane discipline as all other drivers and may only overtake stationary or slow-moving queues under the same conditions that apply to any other vehicle.

motorrad-verkehrsverhalten-03.question: What rule of thumb applies to the safe following distance to the vehicle ahead under normal conditions outside built-up areas?

options.a: The distance in metres should be at least half the speedometer reading in km/h
options.b: One vehicle length is enough at any speed
options.c: Distance does not matter for motorcycles since they brake faster than cars
options.d: It is enough if you can still read the number plate of the vehicle ahead

motorrad-verkehrsverhalten-03.explanation: The well-known 'half your speedometer reading' rule also serves as guidance for motorcyclists to keep enough safe distance so that reaction and braking distance are sufficient in an emergency.

motorrad-verkehrsverhalten-04.question: You are overtaking a long truck on your motorcycle. What should you be particularly prepared for right after passing the tractor unit?

options.a: A sudden strong pull back towards the truck once you have passed it
options.b: A brief sideways gust as you leave the truck's slipstream, which can push the motorcycle sideways
options.c: An automatic drop in the motorcycle's speed
options.d: Nothing in particular, since trucks do not generate relevant airflow

motorrad-verkehrsverhalten-04.explanation: Overtaking large vehicles creates turbulence and a slipstream. Leaving this area can produce a brief sideways gust that pushes the motorcycle off line. Motorcyclists should keep a firm but relaxed grip on the handlebars and leave enough lateral clearance when overtaking.

motorrad-verkehrsverhalten-05.question: Why should you as a motorcyclist be especially cautious at intersections, even when you have right of way?

options.a: Because motorcycles fundamentally have no right of way over cars
options.b: Because motorcycles must always signal at intersections, even when going straight
options.c: Because intersections are legally treated as priority roads for motorcycles
options.d: Because other road users often underestimate a motorcycle's narrow profile and speed, or simply overlook it altogether

motorrad-verkehrsverhalten-05.explanation: Because of its narrow width, a motorcycle's approach speed is frequently misjudged by other road users, and it is easily overlooked. Motorcyclists should therefore stay ready to brake even when they have right of way, and try to make eye contact with other drivers.

motorrad-verkehrsverhalten-06.question: What should you especially pay attention to when riding a motorcycle through a roundabout?

options.a: You must always ride at the far left edge of the roundabout
options.b: Signalling when leaving the roundabout is not required for motorcycles
options.c: Choose a lane position that keeps you clearly visible to following and entering traffic, and signal your exit in good time
options.d: Motorcycles are generally allowed to ride faster than other vehicles in a roundabout

motorrad-verkehrsverhalten-06.explanation: In a roundabout, motorcyclists should choose a clearly visible position, as entering vehicles can easily overlook the narrow profile of a motorcycle. Leaving the roundabout must be signalled in good time.

motorrad-verkehrsverhalten-07.question: What should you pay particular attention to as a motorcyclist when riding in the rain?

options.a: Rain practically does not change the road grip for motorcycles
options.b: Road markings, manhole covers and joints can be noticeably more slippery than the rest of the surface when wet and should be avoided while leaning through a corner
options.c: In rain you should generally ride with more lean angle to get more tyre contact
options.d: Following distance can be reduced in the wet because motorcycles are lighter than cars

motorrad-verkehrsverhalten-07.explanation: Wet road markings, manhole covers, joints and smooth surfaces offer significantly less grip. Motorcyclists should try to cross these upright and at reduced speed to avoid the risk of sliding.

motorrad-verkehrsverhalten-08.question: Why is particular restraint with speed required on a motorcycle at night?

options.a: Because you may only ride as fast as your own headlight allows you to see the road and react to obstacles in time (the 'sight-distance rule')
options.b: Because motorcycles must generally observe a 60 km/h speed limit at night
options.c: Because high beam is legally prohibited on motorcycles
options.d: Because the keep-right rule is generally suspended for motorcycles at night

motorrad-verkehrsverhalten-08.explanation: Under the sight-distance rule, you may only ride as fast as allows you to stop safely within the range illuminated by your own lights. At night this range is much shorter than during the day, so speed must be adjusted accordingly.

motorrad-verkehrsverhalten-09.question: What condition must be met before you may carry a passenger on your motorcycle?

options.a: It is enough if only the rider wears a helmet
options.b: Carrying a passenger is only permitted on motorways
options.c: The motorcycle must be approved for a passenger and fitted with a seat and footrests, and the passenger must also wear a suitable helmet
options.d: The passenger may weigh at most half as much as the rider

motorrad-verkehrsverhalten-09.explanation: Carrying a passenger is only permitted if the vehicle is built and approved for it (seat, footrests) and the passenger wears a helmet. Without these conditions, carrying a passenger is not allowed.

motorrad-verkehrsverhalten-10.question: Are you allowed to tow a trailer behind your motorcycle?

options.a: No, towing a trailer behind a motorcycle is generally prohibited in Germany
options.b: Only if the motorcycle is equipped and approved for it by the manufacturer and the corresponding towing capacity is entered in the vehicle documents
options.c: Yes, with any standard car trailer and no further requirements
options.d: Yes, but only on motorways and other roads reserved for motor vehicles

motorrad-verkehrsverhalten-10.explanation: A trailer may only be towed behind a motorcycle if the vehicle is technically designed and approved for it (e.g. a suitable tow hitch) and the permitted towing weight is entered in the registration document. Without this entry, towing a trailer is not permitted.

motorrad-verkehrsverhalten-11.question: An oncoming car is clearly waiting at the intersection to turn left. How should you behave as a motorcyclist, even though you have right of way?

options.a: You can maintain your speed, since the car has to wait anyway
options.b: You should accelerate to clear the intersection as quickly as possible
options.c: You must sound your horn so the driver is forced to wait
options.d: You should reduce speed as a precaution, stay ready to brake, and try to make eye contact, since turning drivers frequently misjudge a motorcycle's speed and distance

motorrad-verkehrsverhalten-11.explanation: Drivers turning left frequently underestimate the closing speed of oncoming motorcycles because of their narrow profile, which is one of the most common accident patterns for motorcyclists. Anticipating this by staying ready to brake and seeking eye contact significantly improves safety.

motorrad-verkehrsverhalten-12.question: You notice gravel, leaves or tram tracks on the road in a bend. What is the correct way to react?

options.a: Reduce speed before the bend, keep lean angle as low as possible, and avoid any abrupt steering or braking input while on the slippery patch
options.b: Increase your lean angle so the tyres get more contact area on the loose surface
options.c: Brake hard while you are on the loose surface
options.d: Change lanes without checking the traffic behind you

motorrad-verkehrsverhalten-12.explanation: Loose or slick surfaces in a bend significantly reduce tyre grip. Speed should be adjusted beforehand, the bike ridden more upright, and abrupt steering or braking inputs avoided to prevent a fall.

motorrad-verkehrsverhalten-13.question: You are riding past a gap in a forest or a bridge in strong crosswind. What should you be prepared for?

options.a: Such spots have no effect on wind conditions for motorcycles
options.b: A sudden, brief gust that can push the motorcycle sideways, so you should hold the handlebars loosely but securely and adjust your speed
options.c: You should generally accelerate in such areas to get through the wind zone faster
options.d: You should let go of the handlebar grips so the motorcycle stabilises itself

motorrad-verkehrsverhalten-13.explanation: Gaps in woodland, bridges or terrain cuts can produce sudden sideways gusts that push a motorcycle off line. A relaxed but secure grip on the handlebars and a moderate, adjusted speed help to compensate for such gusts.

motorrad-verkehrsverhalten-14.question: Which statement about the helmet requirement on motorcycles is correct?

options.a: The helmet requirement only applies outside built-up areas
options.b: Only the rider must wear a helmet; a passenger is exempt
options.c: Both rider and passenger of a motorcycle must wear a suitable safety helmet while riding
options.d: The helmet requirement does not apply for trips under 50 km/h

motorrad-verkehrsverhalten-14.explanation: While riding a motorcycle, both the rider and any passenger must wear a suitable safety helmet, regardless of speed or distance travelled.

motorrad-verkehrsverhalten-15.question: You stop your motorcycle behind a car at a red light. How should you position yourself?

options.a: As close as possible to the rear of the car, to save space for traffic behind you
options.b: With sufficient distance and slightly offset, so you have an escape route and are visible in the car's rear-view mirror
options.c: Always centred directly behind the car with no safety distance at all
options.d: Generally with your front wheel level with the car, side by side

motorrad-verkehrsverhalten-15.explanation: Keeping enough distance with a slight offset gives the motorcyclist an escape route if a vehicle behind brakes too late, and improves visibility in the mirror of the vehicle ahead.

motorrad-fahrerlaubnis-01.question: What technical limits apply to class A1 motorcycles, and from what age can this class be obtained?

options.a: Up to 250 cc, up to 20 kW, minimum age 18
options.b: Up to 125 cc, up to 11 kW, power-to-weight ratio up to 0.1 kW/kg, minimum age 16
options.c: Up to 50 cc, up to 4 kW, minimum age 15
options.d: No displacement limit, up to 15 kW, minimum age 17

motorrad-fahrerlaubnis-01.explanation: Class A1 covers motorcycles up to 125 cc displacement, a maximum of 11 kW power, and a power-to-weight ratio of no more than 0.1 kW/kg. This licence can be obtained from age 16.

motorrad-fahrerlaubnis-02.question: What restrictions apply to class A2 motorcycles?

options.a: Only a displacement limit of 125 cc applies, power is unrestricted
options.b: There is no power restriction, only a minimum age of 21
options.c: Power must not exceed 35 kW, the power-to-weight ratio must not exceed 0.2 kW/kg, and the motorcycle must not be derived from a version with more than double that power; minimum age is 18
options.d: Power must not exceed 50 kW, minimum age is 20

motorrad-fahrerlaubnis-02.explanation: Class A2 permits motorcycles with a maximum power of 35 kW and a power-to-weight ratio of no more than 0.2 kW/kg. The motorcycle also must not be a restricted version of a model with more than double that original power. The minimum age is 18.

motorrad-fahrerlaubnis-03.question: From what age can the unrestricted class A be obtained directly, without first holding class A2 (so-called direct access)?

options.a: From age 24
options.b: From age 18
options.c: From age 21
options.d: From age 27

motorrad-fahrerlaubnis-03.explanation: Direct access to the unrestricted class A, without previously holding class A2, is possible from a minimum age of 24.

motorrad-fahrerlaubnis-04.question: How can someone who has held class A2 for at least two years obtain class A via the staged access route?

options.a: Automatically upon turning 21, with no further steps required
options.b: From age 20, through a required training certificate, without needing to retake the full theory and practical test
options.c: Only by taking an entirely new theory and practical test, as with direct access
options.d: Only after holding class A2 for at least five years

motorrad-fahrerlaubnis-04.explanation: Anyone who has held class A2 for at least two years can obtain class A via staged access from age 20 by completing a required training course. No new test is needed for this.

motorrad-fahrerlaubnis-05.question: What does the so-called key number 196 on a class B (car) licence enable?

options.a: It automatically authorises the holder to ride all motorcycle classes with no further conditions
options.b: It only applies to motorcycles with a sidecar
options.c: It allows class B holders meeting certain age and licence-holding requirements to ride light motorcycles up to 125 cc within Germany after additional training, without taking a separate A1 test
options.d: It fully replaces class A2, including in other European countries

motorrad-fahrerlaubnis-05.explanation: With key number 196, class B holders who have held the licence for at least five years and meet a minimum age requirement can ride motorcycles up to 125 cc within Germany after completing mandatory additional theory and practical training, without taking a full A1 test. This entitlement is valid only within Germany.

motorrad-fahrerlaubnis-06.question: Which statement about the relationship between motorcycle classes A1, A2 and A is correct?

options.a: Anyone holding class A may also ride motorcycles of classes A1 and A2
options.b: Classes A1, A2 and A each only authorise riding exactly that class
options.c: Class A2 automatically includes class A
options.d: Class A1 automatically also authorises class A2

motorrad-fahrerlaubnis-06.explanation: The higher class A includes the lower classes A1 and A2. Conversely, holding A1 or A2 does not automatically authorise riding the respective higher class.

motorrad-fahrerlaubnis-07.question: What is the minimum legal tread depth for a motorcycle tyre for the vehicle to be used on public roads?

options.a: At least 3.0 mm across the entire tread
options.b: At least 1.6 mm in the main tread grooves
options.c: At least 0.5 mm, since motorcycle tyres need less tread than car tyres
options.d: There is no legally prescribed minimum as long as the tyre visually looks intact

motorrad-fahrerlaubnis-07.explanation: As with car tyres, motorcycle tyres are legally required to have at least 1.6 mm of tread. Since motorcycles have no redundancy from additional wheels compared with cars, sufficient tread for grip and water evacuation is especially safety-critical.

motorrad-fahrerlaubnis-08.question: When should you check your motorcycle's tyre pressure to get a reliable reading?

options.a: Ideally right after a long motorway ride, while the tyres are still warm
options.b: Tyre pressure only needs to be checked once a year at the official vehicle inspection
options.c: Regularly and while the tyres are cold, adjusting the pressure to the manufacturer's specifications and to any extra load or passenger
options.d: Tyre pressure is irrelevant to handling on modern motorcycle tyres

motorrad-fahrerlaubnis-08.explanation: Tyre pressure should be checked regularly while cold, since warm tyres show a higher reading due to heat expansion. Extra load from luggage or a passenger often requires a higher target pressure per the manufacturer's specification, especially at the rear.

motorrad-fahrerlaubnis-09.question: Why is regularly checking chain tension and lubrication on a chain-driven motorcycle safety-critical?

options.a: Incorrect chain tension only affects fuel consumption
options.b: A chain that is too loose or dry can snap or jump off, potentially locking the rear wheel or damaging the casing, which can cause a crash
options.c: Chain tension has no effect on riding safety as long as the chain is oiled
options.d: An overly tight chain automatically extends the engine's lifespan

motorrad-fahrerlaubnis-09.explanation: An insufficiently tensioned or dry chain wears out faster and can snap or jump off the sprocket. This can lock the rear wheel or damage the engine casing, potentially causing a loss of control. Regular checking and lubrication is therefore an important safety check.

motorrad-fahrerlaubnis-10.question: How should you adjust your mirrors before setting off?

options.a: So that part of your own elbow is visible in the mirror, to help judge distance
options.b: Motorcycle mirrors do not need individual adjustment since they are fixed from the factory
options.c: So that you can see as much of the road behind you as possible with minimal head movement, while a shoulder check is still needed to cover the blind spot
options.d: Only the left mirror needs adjusting, the right one is not legally required on motorcycles

motorrad-fahrerlaubnis-10.explanation: Mirrors should be angled to capture as wide an area behind the vehicle as possible with little head movement. Since mirrors cannot fully cover the blind spot, an additional shoulder check remains necessary before changing lanes.

motorrad-fahrerlaubnis-11.question: What areas should be at least checked during a quick visual check before every ride?

options.a: Only the oil level; all other areas are negligible
options.b: Only the lights, since they fail most often
options.c: Only tyre pressure, since it affects handling the most
options.d: Tyres and wheels, controls and brakes, lights, fluid levels such as oil, as well as frame, stands, and that attachments are securely fastened

motorrad-fahrerlaubnis-11.explanation: A brief walk-around before riding should cover tyres, wheels, brakes and controls, the lights, key fluid levels, and that frame components, stands and attachments are securely fastened, so technical defects are spotted early.

motorrad-fahrerlaubnis-12.question: Must motorcycles ride with their lights on during the day in good visibility too?

options.a: Yes, motorcycles must generally ride with dipped headlights even during the day, to be seen more easily
options.b: No, daytime lights are not required for motorcycles and are only recommended in rain
options.c: No, daytime lights are only required on motorways
options.d: Yes, but only with high beam, to achieve maximum visibility

motorrad-fahrerlaubnis-12.explanation: Unlike cars, motorcycles are required to ride with dipped headlights on even during the day in good visibility, since their narrow width makes them significantly harder to notice in traffic.

motorrad-fahrerlaubnis-13.question: Why is it safety-relevant to check that the side or centre stand is fully retracted before setting off?

options.a: An extended stand only prevents the speedometer from displaying correctly
options.b: A stand that is not retracted can touch down while leaning or in a corner, which can lift the rear wheel or bring the motorcycle down
options.c: An extended stand has purely cosmetic effects and no influence at all on riding safety
options.d: An extended stand increases tyre grip while leaning

motorrad-fahrerlaubnis-13.explanation: A stand that has not been retracted can touch the ground while leaning in a corner. This can briefly lift the rear wheel or destabilise the motorcycle and cause a fall, so this should be checked before every ride.

motorrad-fahrerlaubnis-14.question: Why should you test the front and rear brakes at low speed before merging into flowing traffic?

options.a: To determine whether fuel consumption is appropriate
options.b: Because a brake test is legally required only once a year at the official inspection and is otherwise unnecessary
options.c: To confirm a noticeable response and a proper pressure point from both brakes before you have to rely on them in an emergency
options.d: Because doing so automatically readjusts the brake pads

motorrad-fahrerlaubnis-14.explanation: A brief brake test at low speed shows whether the front and rear brakes respond noticeably and have a firm pressure point. This reveals defects before you have to rely on a working brake in an emergency.

motorrad-fahrerlaubnis-15.question: You own a power-restricted ('throttled') motorcycle approved for class A2. Are you allowed to remove the restriction yourself once you feel more confident?

options.a: Yes, the restriction is purely a factory setting with no legal significance
options.b: No, de-restricting changes the vehicle's approved technical data and requires a proper conversion with a corresponding entry in the vehicle documents before the vehicle may be ridden at full power again
options.c: Yes, as long as the de-restriction is undone again within 24 hours
options.d: No, a motorcycle that has once been restricted can never be de-restricted again

motorrad-fahrerlaubnis-15.explanation: The power restriction is part of the vehicle's approval for the relevant licence class. Removing it is a technical modification that must be carried out properly and entered in the vehicle documents before the motorcycle may be used at full power.

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-01.question: Why is riding a motorcycle at night particularly risky with regard to other road users?

options.a: Because motorcycles are generally allowed to ride faster at night
options.b: Because the narrow light pattern and smaller silhouette of a motorcycle make it easier for others to overlook it or misjudge its distance
options.c: Because right-of-way rules do not apply after dark
options.d: Because motorcycles are exempt from lighting requirements at night

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-01.explanation: A single headlight and narrow silhouette make it harder for other drivers to correctly judge a motorcycle's distance and speed. This often leads to dangerous turning or merging situations. Traffic rules do not change at night.

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-02.question: How should you adjust your speed in poor visibility (e.g. dusk, fog)?

options.a: So that you can always stop within the distance you can see to be clear
options.b: It is enough to keep to the posted speed limit
options.c: Riding faster shortens time spent in the hazardous area and is therefore safer
options.d: Speed only needs to be adjusted for rain, not for fog

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-02.explanation: Speed must always be chosen so you can stop within the distance you can see to be clear. In reduced visibility this distance shrinks significantly, regardless of the posted limit.

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-03.question: Which statement about visor and eyewear choice for night riding is correct?

options.a: Tinted visors improve visibility in the dark
options.b: A scratched visor has no effect on vision when facing oncoming lights
options.c: A clear, clean, undamaged visor is important at night, since scratches and tinting increase glare from oncoming vehicles
options.d: You should generally ride without a visor at night to see better

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-03.explanation: Scratches and tinting scatter light and increase glare from oncoming headlights. A clear, undamaged visor is therefore considerably safer for night riding.

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-04.question: How can you further increase your visibility to others at dusk and in darkness?

options.a: By wearing dark clothing so you blend in with the road surface
options.b: By wearing bright or reflective clothing and a light-coloured helmet in addition to the required lighting
options.c: By leaving high beam on permanently, even facing oncoming traffic
options.d: By following closely behind other vehicles to be more visible in their slipstream

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-04.explanation: Bright and reflective clothing plus a visible helmet increase the chance of being noticed early by other road users. High beam must be dipped for oncoming traffic, and tailgating is dangerous and prohibited.

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-05.question: Which road surfaces become especially dangerous for motorcyclists when wet?

options.a: Only freshly asphalted sections without markings
options.b: Only junctions with traffic lights
options.c: Painted road markings, manhole and drain covers, and tram tracks, since they offer significantly less grip when wet
options.d: Only unpaved verges

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-05.explanation: Paint, metal covers and rails are smoother than normal asphalt and become even more slippery when wet. They should be avoided while leaning wherever possible.

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-06.question: Why should you keep a larger following distance in the rain?

options.a: Because braking distance increases on wet roads, and spray from other vehicles further reduces visibility
options.b: Because wet asphalt generally offers more grip than dry asphalt
options.c: Because a motorcycle's brakes automatically switch off in the rain
options.d: Because a larger gap reduces the motorcycle's visibility to others

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-06.explanation: Wetness reduces friction between tyre and road, lengthening the braking distance. Spray thrown up by trucks and cars also reduces visibility, which requires a larger safety gap.

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-07.question: You are riding in the rain and need to take a bend. How should you behave?

options.a: Brake late and hard, then ride faster through the bend
options.b: Reduce speed before the bend, steer in smoothly, and avoid excessive lean angle and abrupt steering or braking inputs while cornering
options.c: Increase your lean angle compared to dry conditions to save time
options.d: Use only the rear brake, since it is supposedly more reliable in the rain

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-07.explanation: Since wet conditions reduce grip, speed should be adjusted before the bend. Within the bend itself, abrupt steering or braking inputs and excessive lean should be avoided to prevent the tyres from losing grip.

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-08.question: Why is the very start of a rain shower after a long dry spell especially treacherous for motorcyclists?

options.a: Because the first rain immediately cleans the road surface fully, making it grippier
options.b: Because riding bans for motorcycles automatically apply during the first minutes of rain
options.c: Because oil, rubber and dust residue mix with the first rain into an especially slippery film before it is washed away
options.d: Because tyres automatically lose tread depth with the first raindrops

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-08.explanation: During dry spells, oil, rubber and dust residue accumulate on the road. The first rain lifts this before it is washed away, creating an especially slippery film. Grip only improves again after sustained rain.

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-09.question: You are riding behind a truck in heavy rain. What particular danger comes from the spray it throws up?

options.a: It can briefly almost completely block your view through the visor, so a larger gap or a cautious overtake is advisable
options.b: It improves visibility because it cleans the motorcycle's windscreen
options.c: It has no effect on visibility at all, only on tyre grip
options.d: It only occurs on dry roads

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-09.explanation: Trucks throw up large amounts of spray in the rain, which can briefly blind motorcyclists or severely reduce visibility. A larger gap and decisive, well-planned overtaking reduce this risk.

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-10.question: Why do motorcycle tyres need some time after setting off in cold weather before reaching full grip?

options.a: Because cold tyres generally need more air pressure than warm ones
options.b: Because the rubber is harder at low temperatures and only reaches the operating temperature needed for optimal grip through flexing and motion
options.c: Because tyres automatically gain deeper tread in cold weather
options.d: Because cold tyres only lose grip on motorways

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-10.explanation: Cold tyre rubber is harder and offers less grip. Only through flexing while riding does the tyre warm up and reach optimal grip. In the first few minutes, strong lean angles and hard braking should therefore be avoided.

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-11.question: Where does black ice tend to form most easily around freezing temperatures, making it hard for motorcyclists to spot?

options.a: Only on wide, busy main roads in city centres
options.b: Only in spots with direct sunlight
options.c: On bridges, in shaded wooded stretches and on damp patches, which cool fastest and often freeze into a nearly invisible, glassy layer
options.d: Only on unpaved tracks

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-11.explanation: Bridges cool from both sides and therefore freeze earlier than the surrounding road. Shaded, damp spots also cool faster. Black ice there is often nearly invisible and can easily be mistaken for a merely wet surface.

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-12.question: How can cold indirectly impair a motorcyclist's riding safety?

options.a: Because cold, stiff fingers reduce fine control over clutch, brake and throttle and can lengthen reaction time
options.b: Because cold automatically deactivates the brake light
options.c: Because motorcycles are generally required to ride at a lower maximum speed in cold weather
options.d: Because cold air improves visibility through the visor

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-12.explanation: Cold reduces finger mobility and fine motor control, making it harder to modulate the brake and clutch precisely, which can limit responsiveness in critical situations. Suitable warm gloves are therefore important.

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-13.question: You set off on your motorcycle on a cold winter morning. How should you ride in the first few minutes?

options.a: Immediately ride at full lean and high speed, otherwise the engine will not warm up
options.b: Ride cautiously, at moderate speed and with little lean angle, until tyres, chassis and your own concentration have adjusted to conditions
options.c: Use the brakes as little as possible to preserve them
options.d: Head straight onto the motorway, since it is generally less snowy there

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-13.explanation: Cold tyres and a body that may not yet be fully warmed up call for extra caution in the first few minutes of riding. Speed and lean angle should be increased gradually once conditions prove safe.

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-14.question: Why is leaf litter on the road in autumn especially dangerous for motorcyclists when combined with moisture?

options.a: Because wet leaves give the tyres extra grip
options.b: Because leaves generally protect the road surface from becoming slippery
options.c: Because damp leaves can form a very slippery, almost soap-like layer offering very little grip, especially when cornering or braking
options.d: Because dry leaves improve braking performance

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-14.explanation: Damp leaves can act almost like a lubricating layer and drastically reduce grip. On leaf-covered stretches, speed and lean angle should be significantly reduced, especially when cornering or braking.

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-15.question: What fundamentally changes in your motorcycle's handling when you carry a pillion passenger?

options.a: Nothing, the extra weight is automatically compensated for by ABS
options.b: Centre of gravity, acceleration, braking and cornering behaviour all change noticeably due to the added weight and its distribution
options.c: The motorcycle only becomes easier to handle, since the passenger improves balance
options.d: Braking distance shortens because of the extra weight on the rear wheel

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-15.explanation: A pillion significantly changes the motorcycle's centre of gravity and total weight. Acceleration becomes more sluggish, braking distance typically increases, and cornering behaviour changes. Riders must adapt to this.

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-16.question: What must a motorcycle have for a pillion passenger to be carried legally?

options.a: It must have a proper second seat and footrests for the passenger
options.b: It is sufficient for the passenger to hold on to the rider with both hands
options.c: A second seat is sufficient; footrests are not legally required
options.d: It is enough for the passenger to ride on the luggage rack without a seat

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-16.explanation: To carry a pillion passenger, the motorcycle must be fitted with a proper seat and footrests intended for the passenger. Carrying someone without this equipment is not permitted.

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-17.question: What is the rider's responsibility before riding with an inexperienced pillion passenger for the first time?

options.a: None, the passenger must find out the correct behaviour themselves
options.b: Only to tell the passenger where the helmet is located
options.c: To brief the passenger on appropriate behaviour, e.g. leaning with the bike in corners, holding on, sitting still and using the footrests
options.d: The rider may only instruct the passenger after setting off

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-17.explanation: An inexperienced passenger can seriously disturb stability through incorrect behaviour, such as leaning against the bike in corners or moving abruptly. A brief briefing before setting off significantly improves safety for both.

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-18.question: What equipment requirement applies to a motorcycle pillion passenger as well?

options.a: The passenger must wear a suitable protective helmet, just like the rider
options.b: The passenger does not need a helmet since only the rider is responsible for riding safety
options.c: A bicycle helmet is sufficient for the passenger
options.d: Helmet requirements for the passenger only apply outside built-up areas

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-18.explanation: The helmet requirement applies equally to rider and passenger, regardless of road type. A helmet approved for road use is required; a bicycle helmet does not meet this requirement.

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-19.question: How does a pillion passenger typically affect the motorcycle's braking behaviour?

options.a: Braking distance always shortens noticeably
options.b: The higher total weight tends to increase braking distance, so braking should start earlier and be more anticipatory
options.c: Braking behaviour is completely unchanged in every case
options.d: Only the front brake is affected by a pillion, not the rear brake

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-19.explanation: With the added weight of a passenger, braking distance generally increases. Riders should compensate by braking earlier and anticipating hazards, and by keeping a larger safety gap.

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-20.question: How should you ride through roadworks with uneven surfaces, gravel or a road-level offset?

options.a: Ride through as quickly as possible to shorten the hazardous stretch
options.b: Brake hard while crossing a road-level offset to stay in control
options.c: Reduce speed significantly, ride upright with a relaxed upper body, and complete braking before reaching uneven sections
options.d: Always avoid the middle of the lane and instead ride at the very edge of the roadworks

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-20.explanation: In roadworks with uneven surfaces, gravel or offsets, speed should be reduced and the bike ridden as upright as possible. Braking should be completed before the uneven section, since braking on loose surfaces endangers stability.

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-21.question: Why are loose gravel or chippings, as often found in roadworks or on freshly patched road sections, particularly critical for motorcycles?

options.a: Because they reduce tyre wear
options.b: Because loose material between tyre and road can act like tiny ball bearings, drastically reducing grip when braking, accelerating or cornering
options.c: Because they only affect visibility, not tyre grip
options.d: Because gravel is harmless for motorcycles as long as speed is above 80 km/h

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-21.explanation: Loose chippings greatly reduce direct contact between the tyre and the solid road surface. This markedly lowers grip, especially during braking, accelerating or steering inputs, increasing the risk of a fall.

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-22.question: You are approaching a road section with pronounced ruts and undulations. What is the correct way to behave?

options.a: Adjust your speed, choose a line that avoids deep ruts where possible, and make steering movements calm and controlled
options.b: Ride through as fast as possible so the motorcycle skips over the bumps
options.c: Ride right in the middle of the rut, since that provides the most stable path
options.d: Take your hands off the handlebar to avoid vibrations

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-22.explanation: Ruts can pull the front wheel sideways and affect steering. Adjusted speed, a carefully chosen line and calm steering inputs help keep the motorcycle under control.

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-23.question: How should you behave in strong, gusty crosswinds, e.g. on open stretches or bridges?

options.a: Ride as fast as possible to spend less time exposed to the wind
options.b: Reduce speed, hold the handlebar firmly but relaxed, and be prepared for sudden gusts, especially where wind shelter from trees, bridge piers or trucks suddenly ends
options.c: Grip the handlebar as rigidly as possible to fully suppress the effect of gusts
options.d: Always ride at the very right edge of the lane, regardless of the rest of the traffic

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-23.explanation: In gusty crosswinds the motorcycle can suddenly be pushed sideways, especially where shelter from wind (e.g. trees or bridge piers) ends abruptly. Reduced speed and a relaxed but secure grip allow gusts to be absorbed rather than fought rigidly.

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-24.question: What is the so-called bow wave (pressure wave) of a passing or overtaking truck, and how should you react to it?

options.a: It only affects the truck driver and has no effect on other vehicles
options.b: It only occurs in the rain and can be ignored
options.c: It is a brief turbulence of air that can push the motorcycle sideways or pull it into a suction effect; riders should hold the handlebar securely and keep sufficient lateral distance from the truck
options.d: It can be completely avoided by riding faster

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-24.explanation: Large vehicles like trucks create a pressure wave as they pass, followed by a suction effect. This can briefly push or pull a motorcycle off its line. A secure grip, adjusted speed and greater lateral distance help absorb this.

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-25.question: Why should motorcyclists be especially cautious when overtaking a truck in strong crosswind?

options.a: Because trucks are generally required to reduce speed to 30 km/h in crosswind
options.b: Because the wind shelter provided by the truck changes suddenly at its end, and the motorcycle can be hit by a gust without warning
options.c: Because motorcycles are automatically shielded from crosswind while overtaking
options.d: Because crosswind is only relevant when riding behind a vehicle, not when overtaking it

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-25.explanation: While overtaking, the truck briefly shields the motorcycle from crosswind. As soon as the motorcycle reaches the front of the truck or passes it, an unexpected gust can occur, for which the rider should be prepared.

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-26.question: Why is fatigue especially dangerous for motorcyclists, even more so than for car drivers?

options.a: Because motorcycles automatically slow down when the rider is tired
options.b: Because fatigue has no relevant effect on motorcycling, since the vehicle keeps its lane by itself
options.c: Because a motorcycle must be actively balanced, so even a brief lapse in concentration or a micro-sleep can lead to a loss of control and a fall
options.d: Because fatigue can only occur during night rides

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-26.explanation: Unlike a four-wheeled vehicle, a motorcycle does not remain stable on its own. A brief micro-sleep or lapse in concentration can immediately cause a loss of balance and a fall. Fatigue is therefore especially risky for single-track vehicles.

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-27.question: On a longer ride you notice early signs of fatigue, such as heavy eyelids and reduced concentration. What is correct?

options.a: Take a break as soon as possible, get off the bike and rest or move around if needed, before continuing the ride
options.b: Increase speed to reach the destination faster and shorten the period of fatigue
options.c: Open the visor and keep riding, since fresh air completely eliminates fatigue
options.d: Turn up music through a headset and keep riding without a break

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-27.explanation: Early signs of fatigue should be taken seriously. Since motorcycling requires actively maintaining balance, taking a timely break is much safer than trying to mask fatigue with distraction or higher speed.

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-28.question: Which statement about anti-lock braking systems (ABS) on motorcycles is correct?

options.a: ABS generally prevents any fall, regardless of road conditions
options.b: ABS prevents the wheels from locking during hard braking and often shortens braking distance, but it does not replace riding adapted to conditions
options.c: ABS only works in wet conditions and is ineffective on dry roads
options.d: ABS generally increases the maximum lean angle possible in corners

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-28.explanation: ABS prevents wheel lock and helps maintain control during emergency braking. However, it cannot overcome the physical limits of tyre grip and does not replace anticipatory, condition-adapted riding.

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-29.question: On which surfaces can ABS and traction control reach their physical limits, meaning riders should not blindly rely on them?

options.a: Only on dry asphalt at moderate speed
options.b: Only on motorways with continuous lane markings
options.c: On very low-grip surfaces such as black ice, loose gravel, mud or spilled oil, where there is barely any grip even with electronic assistance
options.d: Only when riding with a pillion passenger, never when riding alone

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-29.explanation: ABS and traction control can only make optimal use of the grip that exists, but cannot create additional grip. On extremely slippery surfaces such as black ice, oil or loose gravel, the risk of a fall remains high despite these systems.

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-30.question: What role does traction control play when accelerating under special conditions, e.g. on a wet or slippery road?

options.a: It can detect rear-wheel spin during acceleration and reduce power, but it does not replace careful, condition-adapted throttle control
options.b: It generally prevents any loss of grip, regardless of road conditions
options.c: It is only relevant for racetrack use and has no function in road traffic
options.d: It completely removes the need to adjust speed for wet or slippery conditions

motorrad-besondere_bedingungen-30.explanation: Traction control helps detect rear-wheel spin and adjusts engine power accordingly. However, it cannot overcome the physical limits of tyre grip, so careful, situation-adapted riding remains essential.
